thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Dow Slip Ahead Of Fed, But Nasdaq Buoyed By Apple's Stock Rally

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500, Dow Slip Ahead Of Fed, But Nasdaq Buoyed By Apple's Stock Rally
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Wall Street set to pore over Federal Open Market Committee update for clues about inflation, economic expansion
U.S. stocks mostly traded lower Wednesday, as a blowout quarter at Apple wasn't enough to overshadow caution over an coming statement by the Federal Reserve.
While the Fed isn't expected to announce any changes to interest rates at the end of its two-day meeting Wednesday afternoon, the possibility of any update to forward-looking central bank policy is widely seen as one of the most consequential factors behind trading today.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 60 points to 24,042, a decline of 0.2%. The S&P 500 index lost 6 points, or 0.2%, to 2,648. The Nasdaq Composite Index added 4 points to 7,135, an advance of 0.1%.
If the Dow closes in negative territory, that will mark its fourth straight daily drop. It has fallen in nine of the past 11 sessions, including Wednesday.
What's driving markets?
Apple's stock (AAPL)rose 4.3% after the largest U.S. company by market capitalization late Tuesday posted better-than-anticipated earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-rises-after-iphone-sales-fall-short-but-earnings-beat-2018-05-01) for the first quarter. As the largest stock in the economy, based on market capitalization, the move limited the overall decline of major indexes.
Check out:Apple earnings were saved by the company's new MVP (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-were-saved-by-the-companys-new-mvp-2018-05-01)
And see: The surprise in Apple earnings--big growth in China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01)
The iPhone maker was merely the latest high-profile company to top analyst forecasts in its results. However, even better-than-expected earnings haven't been enough to lift the main equity benchmarks out of a tight range in recent weeks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-bulls-lose-hope-as-indexes-trade-in-a-tight-range-2018-04-24), as investors are also worried about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
Which economic releases are on tap?
Fed officials are due to wrap up a two-day meeting, and the policy makers are expected to leave interest rates on hold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/as-market-churns-fed-will-say-it-has-inflation-situation-under-control-2018-04-26). Market participants are watching for any change to plans for a tightening path of two more rate increases in 2018. Changes to Fed policy--including both higher rates and a shrinking balance sheet--are seen as one of the primary risks to stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/forget-trade-heres-the-real-risk-to-the-stock-market-2018-04-05) over the remainder of the year.
The Federal Open Market Committee's policy statement is slated to hit at 2 p.m. Eastern Time.
Don't miss: Why the Fed could make 4 rate hikes this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-will-make-4-rate-hikes-this-year-economists-say-after-latest-gdp-eci-reports-2018-04-27)
In the latest economic data, the private sector added 204,000 jobs in April (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-204000-private-sector-jobs-in-april-adp-2018-05-02), according to ADP. While this was above forecasts, it was also down from the 241,000 added in the previous month.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are market analysts saying?
"Market expectations for this Fed meeting are straightforward. No rate hike on Wednesday, but a more hawkish communiqué," said Nicholas Colas, co-founder of DataTrek Research.
"What matters more to markets is this question: 'Where will fed funds be at the end of 2019?' Will we have to relive the '3 vs. 4 rate increases' debate next year as well? This hasn't been a friendly narrative for U.S. stocks this year, although high valuations and twitchy long-term rates haven't helped either.
Which stocks are in focus?
In addition to Apple, quarterly earnings remain a primary focus for investors.
Snap Inc.(SNAP) plummeted 18% a day after reporting revenue and active daily users that were below forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/snap-redesign-flops-sending-stock-down-19-as-analysts-slash-targets-2018-05-02).
Yum Brands Inc. (YUM) reported first-quarter earnings and sales that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/yum-brands-tops-earnings-estimates-backs-2018-guidance-2018-05-02). The fast-food chain operator also affirmed its full-year guidance. Shares fell 5.8%.
CVS Health Corp.(CVS) fell 3.2% despite reporting adjusted first-quarter earnings that beat expectations, along with better-than-expected sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cvs-shares-rise-after-profit-beats-views-2018-05-02).
Southern Co.(SO) reported first-quarter revenue that beat expectations, and earnings that were helped by the recently passed tax bill (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/southern-co-profit-boosted-by-tax-revamp-2018-05-02). The stock rose 0.6%.
Madison Square Garden Co. (MSG) swung to a first-quarter profit and reported revenue that topped analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/madison-square-garden-surprises-with-profit-and-revenue-beat-2018-05-02). The stock rose 1.5%.
Wyndham Worldwide Corp.(WYN) reported a sharp drop in its first-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wyndham-worldwide-profit-falls-62-2018-05-02), although sales rose modestly. Shares fell 4%.
SodaStream International Ltd.(SODA) reported first-quarter earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sodastream-shares-jump-after-earnings-beat-and-guidance-raised-2018-05-02). It also raised its outlook. However, the stock lost 4.5%.
After the market closes, earnings releases should come from Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) and Tesla Inc. (TSLA), among others.
Esperion Therapeutics Inc.(ESPR) announced results for a late-stage clinical trial (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/esperion-shares-halted-on-positive-late-stage-trial-results-2018-05-02) of its cholesterol-lowering medication. The stock plummeted 26%.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks rose modestly, supported by upbeat corporate results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-upbeat-corporate-updates-roll-in-2018-05-02). U.K. stocks added 0.4%.
Markets in Asia were little changed. Stocks in Japan dipped 0.2%. Investors were awaiting cues from U.S.-China trade negotiations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-quiet-awaiting-upcoming-economic-data-2018-05-01), along with the release of both a raft of April manufacturing data from Asia and the Federal Reserve's latest policy statement.
Gold futures rose 0.3%, while oil futures also gained about 0.3%. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index fell less than 0.1% a day after turning positive for 2018.
